subject: Request: evidence for model-training exclusion & prompt/response retention
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@bluebayhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: security@bluebayhealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial security questions for LLM pilot (training / retention)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo last week. BlueBay is evaluating Redwood for a small clinical documentation pilot and our security team has a few clarifying questions before we can proceed to legal/procurement. Can you confirm the following and provide evidence/artifacts where possible?

1) Model training: Will customer-provided content (prompts, uploads, responses, or logs) ever be used to further train or fine-tune Redwood models? If yes, what opt-out mechanism exists?

2) Prompt/response storage: How long are prompts and model responses retained by default in the hosted API? Where are these stored, and are they encrypted at rest/in transit? Can retention be configured per-customer to 0 days?

3) Evidence: We need (a) a short attestation statement addressing #1 and #2, (b) a DPIA or equivalent data-flow diagram for the hosted API, and (c) a list of SOC 2 or ISO artifacts you can share under NDA.

BlueBay will need answers within 3 business days to keep our procurement timeline. I’ve attached our AI security questionnaire for reference.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Information Security
BlueBay Health

Attachments: BlueBay_AI-Security-Questionnaire_2027.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@bluebayhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial security questions for LLM pilot (training / retention)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the clear list and for the quick timeline. Short answers up front so you have something to share immediately:

- Training on customer content: By default, Redwood does NOT use customer content from hosted API requests to train or improve our public model weights. Customers may opt in to a voluntary data-sharing program for product improvements; that is explicit, documented, and requires affirmative action by the customer. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer content is never used for model training.

- Prompt/response storage: Default retention for hosted API request/response payloads is 30 days for debugging and abuse-detection purposes. Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256). For enterprise customers we offer configurable retention (including immediate purge / 0-day retention) and the ability to route logs to customer-managed storage (S3 in their account) via our Dedicated offering.

- Evidence: I’m attaching our short "Model Exclusion Playbook" and a retention matrix that maps defaults and configurable options. For SOC 2 / ISO artifacts we can share the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a SOC control mapping.

Next steps: if you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our security & compliance lead to walk through the questionnaire and confirm the DPIA sketch. Will that work for your team this week?

I’ve attached: redwood-model-exclusion-playbook.pdf, retention_matrix_2027.xlsx

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Security (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-model-exclusion-playbook.pdf; retention_matrix_2027.xlsx

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Initial security questions for LLM pilot (training / retention)

Vivek / Monica —

Draft attestation language we should send to BlueBay (keeps legal review light):

"Redwood Inference attests that customer content submitted to Redwood-hosted APIs is not used to train or update Redwood public model weights unless the customer explicitly opts in to our data-sharing program. For Dedicated and Private deployments, Redwood never uses customer content to train models. Redwood retains request/response payloads for up to 30 days by default for operational troubleshooting and abuse detection; retention can be reduced to 0 days or configured to export into customer-managed storage. All data is encrypted in transit and at rest. SOC 2 Type II reports and selected supporting artifacts are available under a standard NDA."

Evidence checklist to bundle:
- Short attestation (as above)
- Model Exclusion Playbook (internal control steps + logs we use to prove exclusion)
- Retention matrix (default vs configurable)
- DPIA/dataflow diagram (redacted for public sharing; full under NDA)
- SOC 2 Type II report (NDA)

Technical notes to include in the DPIA: KMS key rotation schedule, S3 bucket patterns for request logs (redacted), queue retention settings, and the cluster-level isolation policy for Dedicated pools.

If you want I’ll spin a redlined DPIA checklist and a one-page control mapping to SOC 2 (CC6, CC7 equivalents).

- Rishi

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@bluebayhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, security@bluebayhealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial security questions for LLM pilot (training / retention)

Hi Sofia —

Following up with a consolidated response and attachments. Thank you for the patience while we collected the artifacts.

1) Model training / opt-out
We confirm that Redwood does not use customer-provided content submitted to our hosted API to train or fine-tune public model weights unless a customer explicitly opts into our data-sharing program. Opt-in is documented, logged, and reversible. For Dedicated (reserved) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, customer content is never used for model training by Redwood.

2) Prompt/response retention
- Default: hosted API request and response payloads are retained for up to 30 days for debugging, abuse detection, and service operation.
- Configurability: enterprise customers can reduce retention to 0 days, enable immediate purge, or configure delivery of logs to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS) in Dedicated/Private modes.
- Protections: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest; per-customer KMS options available for Dedicated/Private. Access to stored payloads is logged and scoped by RBAC.

3) Evidence and artifacts (attached / available)
- Short attestation: included in this email (see below).
- Model Exclusion Playbook (attached): internal controls and proof steps we use to demonstrate a customer was excluded from training.
- Retention matrix (attached): default and configurable retention options and where data may be exported.
- DPIA / data flow: sketch included; full DPIA and the SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.

Attestation (official):
"Redwood Inference attests that customer content provided to Redwood-hosted services is not used to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood public model weights unless the customer explicitly opts in to our data sharing program. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer content is never used to train models. Request/response retention is configurable; default retention for hosted APIs is 30 days, and enterprise configurations can set retention to 0 days or use customer-managed storage. Redwood encrypts data in transit and at rest, maintains controls for access and auditing, and can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence under NDA."

Next steps: I can share the SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted DPIA as soon as we have an NDA in place. Would you like us to prepare the NDA and schedule a 30-minute call with our security engineering lead this week?

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Security (acting)
Redwood Inference
